subject: Zenith Health — latency windowing, measurement methodology, and service credit examples
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Anna Weston <anna.weston@zenithhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@zenithhealth.com, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Zenith Health — initial SLO evidence and measurement notes

Hi Anna,

Thanks for the RFP items on SLOs — attached are the evidence pack and a measurement matrix that map our SLA language to telemetry artifacts.

High-level measurement approach:
- Uptime: calculated per-route as the percent of probe+production-successful requests over the billing window. We use a moving 30-day window for monthly SLA checks and a 24-hour burst window for short outages.
- Latency: p95 and p99 measured on user-facing requests at ingress, excluding cache hits (we include cache hit rate as a separate metric). Windows are computed per-hour and aggregated to daily and monthly percentiles using weighted sampling to avoid spike skew.
- Sampling & telemetry: 100% sampling for error traces and 1% for successful requests; automatic ramping to 10% when error rate increases above threshold.
- Attribution: We attribute failures to Redwood when server-side errors or probe failures occur; upstream network issues are excluded where we can correlate with cloud provider events.
- Service credits: credits are calculated as percentage of monthly invoice prorated by duration and severity bucket. Examples included in the attached calculator.

Attachments:
- ZNH-SLO-Evidence-Pack.pdf (evidence index, example dashboards, retention windows)
- measurement-matrix.xlsx (metric -> source -> query)

Next steps: can we schedule a 45-minute call to walk the measurement examples and run through two outage scenarios? I can do Oct 23 between 10:00-12:00 PT or Oct 24 14:00-17:00 PT.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments — helpful. A few clarifying items before we schedule:
1) Burst windows: when you say a 24-hour burst window, does that mean a contiguous outage of X minutes within 24 hours or an aggregated set of small incidents? Our legal team is sensitive to aggregated micro-failures summing to a large credit.
2) Cache exclusions: we rely heavily on in-memory result caching in our app tier. For latency p99/p95, will Redwood exclude cache hits entirely or provide parallel metrics (with-cache / without-cache)? We need reproducible dashboards.
3) Dedicated vs Private: do the same telemetry and crediting rules apply to Dedicated pools and Private (VPC/on-prem)? If Private, we may need a self-attestation or log bundle to validate credits.
4) Can you provide a sample telemetry screenshot or query for the p99 calculation? Also interested in the exact rollup window (hourly median of minute p99s vs direct monthly p99).

Also: procurement asked about how service credits are applied when a customer uses both Hosted and Dedicated routes.

If you can include short examples and an explicit credit calc table I can pass these to legal/procurement.

Anna's four bullets look like the ones we usually get — proposed short answers below for Alex to send back. I also attached a one-line crediting-calculator that maps severity/duration -> percent of monthly invoice.

1) Burst window definition: propose this wording — "Burst window is a 24-hour rolling window used for short outage detection. For credit calculations, incidents are considered contiguous when two outage events are separated by less than 5 minutes; otherwise they are separate incidents and credited independently." The 5-minute stitch rule prevents micro-flapping from inflating credit.

2) Cache handling: provide both metrics. We'll deliver p99_user_requests_excluding_cache and p99_user_requests_including_cache. Exclusion is implemented by tagging requests at ingress when cache-hit header is present. Both series will be in measurement-matrix.xlsx.

3) Dedicated vs Private: Dedicated: Redwood runs the same telemetry and applies credits per the contract. Private (VPC/on-prem): by default we provide the measurement queries, raw log bundles (redacted as needed), and an attestation report. If the customer wants Redwood-run measurement for Private, add a monitoring add-on in the contract.

4) Rollup method: recommend "hourly p99 computed across all successful user requests (excluding cache) -> daily p99 via weighted median of hourly p99s -> monthly p99 as the 30-day rolling percentile." We should include a query snippet for PromQL and an example Grafana screenshot.

Examples: attached CSV shows three scenarios with numbers and final credit percent.

Alex — if this looks good I can tidy and send to Anna with attachments and the drive link to example dashboards.

Subject: Zenith Health — finalized measurement definitions and sample credit calculations

Hi Anna,

Thanks for the questions — we reviewed internally and documented the precise definitions below. I've also uploaded a short walkthrough to the Drive link and attached the crediting CSV.

Definitions (final):
- Uptime (Availability): percent of successful HTTP 2xx/3xx responses to user-facing API endpoints measured by combined production telemetry and our global probe network. Measurement window: 30-day rolling window for monthly SLA; 24-hour rolling "burst" window used to detect short outages for operational response.
- Burst aggregation rule: two outage events within 5 minutes are stitched and treated as one contiguous incident for crediting.
- Latency: p95 and p99 computed on user-facing requests at ingress. We publish two series: p99_excluding_cache (requests with cache-hint header absent) and p99_including_cache. Exclusion is performed at ingress tagging time, so gaps in cache instrumentation do not affect the excluded series.
- Rollup algorithm: hourly p99 computed on raw request samples -> daily p99 via weighted median of hourly p99s -> monthly p99 as 30-day rolling percentile. We include a PromQL snippet in the Drive folder.
- Sampling & spike handling: 100% sampling for error traces, default 1% for successful requests with automatic ramping to 10% when error rate > 0.5% for a 5-minute window. Sampling changes are deterministic and recorded in the trace metadata.

Service credit examples (simplified):
- Severity S1 (complete ingress outage): > 99.9% downtime in a 1-hour window -> credit = 10% of monthly invoice for the hour affected, capped at 50% monthly.
- Severity S2 (partial degradation, elevated p99): sustained p99_excluding_cache > 2s for 6 consecutive hours -> credit = 5% of monthly invoice for that 6-hour window, prorated.
- Aggregation: credits for multiple incidents in a billing month sum until the monthly cap. The attached CSV contains worked examples with numbers for a $50k monthly invoice.

Dedicated vs Private:
- Dedicated pools: Redwood measures and applies credits per the same methodology; credits are applied against the Dedicated invoice.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Redwood provides the same measurement queries, raw logs, and an attestation package. Redwood-operated measurement and crediting for Private is available as an add-on and can be included in the contract.

Deliverables attached/linked:
- ZNH-SLO-Evidence-Pack.pdf (detailed artifacts and retention)
- measurement-matrix.xlsx (metric -> source -> query)
- crediting-calculator.csv (worked examples)
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3ZNH-evidence (example dashboards, PromQL snippets)

Next steps: please confirm which day/time works for a 45-minute walkthrough (Oct 27 09:00-11:00 PT or Oct 28 13:00-16:00 PT) and share the legal/procurement contact for final contract language. Also tell us whether you want Redwood to include Dedicated metrics on a single invoice or split them; we can accommodate either.

Looking forward to the walkthrough.
